To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fat and disabled people find happiness in the spaces in-between the biopedagogical requirements of happiness, and that this alterity in/of their happiness is both joyful and angry.
the requirement to be a happy citizen in a neoliberal society is an impossible task.

fat and disabled subjects are taught to appear as if they are happy, through biopedagogic discourses, to manage shame and to avoid the disgust evoked by the unruly and non-conforming nature of their bodies, while at the same times, creating moments of happiness in/of difference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how disabled and fat bodies are taught to appear as “happy” through biopedagogical practices and how we might resist these demands by creating and finding happiness in/of difference.
how fat and disabled people are taught to be happy and the ways in which they resist this teaching.

the ways that disabled and fat people are taught to appear as “happy” through biopedagogical practices, and how we find and create happiness in/of alterity, in spite of the shame and disgust evoking unruly bodies we are forced to inhabit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
happiness, in its current form, is not enough.
happiness can be found in difference.
happiness is not a state of being but rather an action, and that it can be a radical and political action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are exploring the radical possibilities that emerge from the intersection of happiness and disability.
we explore how disabled and fat bodies can be happy, but not necessarily in the way that is expected or desired of us.
we are interested in how happiness is a site of resistance for those of us who are fat and disabled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the requirement to be “happy” is not just a requirement to appear happy, but also a requirement to be happy.
happiness is not a universal state, but rather is a state of mind, which is always already in relation to other bodies and minds, and is therefore always already a relational state of being.
we can and do live in happiness, despite the requirement to appear as happy.
